title: Model sourcing resilience and latency/cost arbitrage scenarios
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Produce a decision-ready playbook that helps Redwood product and GTM teams choose model-sourcing strategies across regions and customer tiers under realistic outage/availability and latency/cost trade-offs.

Scope:
- Competitive landscape map for 12 months (open models, hosted vendors, managed offerings) with availability risk scoring by region.
- Scenario catalog (3 severity levels) for supply shocks: provider outage, model deprecation, regional capacity shortage.
- Latency/cost arbitrage matrix: when to route to cheaper quantized variants vs higher-quality unquantized replicas (per use-case).
- Procurement trigger matrix: signal thresholds (latency percentile, cost per token, error rate, SLA breach) that recommend actions (reroute, increase reserved capacity, procure alternate model family).
- Quick-reference fallback families and compatibility notes (tokenizer differences, API call surface, structured output regressions).

Deliverables:
1) Playbook doc with decision trees and sample runbooks for NOC/SEs.
2) A regional availability heatmap and time-to-fallback estimates.
3) Benchmarks: latency and cost samples for 5 model family variants across three regions at typical load profiles.
4) A prioritized list of supplier integration tasks (API adapters, tokenizer normalization, eval suites).

Key trade-offs and initial hypotheses:
- Prefer local low-latency models for latency-critical features even at 10–20% higher unit cost; prefer global cheaper variants for background batch work.
- Aggressive quantization reduces cost but increases hallucination risk for structured outputs; risk threshold depends on feature SLA.
- Reserving Dedicated capacity reduces latency variance but increases fixed costs; recommend hybrid reserved+burst strategy for mid-market customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook reviewed and approved by PM leads (Priya Desai) and two engineers (Marcus Li, Elena Rodriguez).
- Benchmarks reproducible by ENG with scripts and PRs linked.
- Procurement triggers mapped to console alerts and a PagerDuty runbook.

Notes on scope exclusions:
- Does not include legal procurement terms; will hand off to Procurement for contract language.
- On-prem installer/ops playbooks are listed but outside the first deliverable (follow-up).
